title: Make edit-tool matching independent of CRLF versus LF line endings
before: At parent 65fb9116, the edit tool compared oldText directly with raw file content using includes, split, and indexOf. An LF-only oldText therefore did not match equivalent text stored with Windows CRLF line endings. Replacement output and diffs also operated directly on raw content.
after: At c214a334, the edit tool detects the file's line-ending style, normalizes file content, oldText, and newText to LF for matching, uniqueness checks, replacement, and diff generation, then converts the completed content back to the detected CRLF or LF style before writing. LF-only model input can edit CRLF files while ordinary CRLF and LF files retain their respective line-ending styles.
diff: Added detectLineEnding, normalizeToLF, and restoreLineEndings helpers. Reworked existence checks, occurrence counting, index calculation, replacement, and no-op detection to use normalized strings. Restored the detected file style at the write boundary and generated diffs from normalized content. Simplified the success message by removing raw character counts. Added four tests covering LF input against CRLF content, CRLF preservation, LF preservation, and duplicate detection across mixed CRLF/LF variants.
call_sites: The changed edit implementation is used by the default mutable coding tool set, the all-tools map, and working-directory-specific createCodingTools/createAllTools factories, so the normalization applies to standard agent edit operations without call-site changes.
tests: A regression test writes CRLF content and invokes editTool with LF-only oldText/newText, asserting that the edit succeeds.
Regression tests read the resulting files and assert that a CRLF file remains entirely CRLF after editing and an LF file remains LF.
A regression test creates logically duplicated text using one CRLF occurrence and one LF occurrence, then verifies that normalized uniqueness checking reports two occurrences.

title: Decode Win32 folder-picker paths without a fixed-size unmanaged view
before: The Win32 directory-picker binding decoded the NUL-terminated UTF-16 path returned by IShellItem::GetDisplayName by creating a fixed 32,768-byte Koffi external view, scanning that view for a two-byte NUL terminator, and converting the prefix with Buffer.toString('utf16le'). The fixed view neither represented the allocation's actual size nor supported paths whose encoded data exceeded 32 KiB.
after: The binding serializes the BigInt native string address into an eight-byte buffer, restricts the buffer to the process pointer width reported by koffi.sizeof('void *'), and passes that pointer variable to koffi.decode(..., 'str16'). The resultPath path still frees the original GetDisplayName address with CoTaskMemFree and releases the shell item. Tests cover four- and eight-byte pointer preservation, the original release address, BMP characters with zero low bytes, surrogate pairs, NUL termination, and strings longer than 32 KiB using real Koffi decoding over live test-owned buffers.
diff: Removed Koffi.view from the local binding interface and replaced the fixed external-memory view plus manual UTF-16 terminator scan with pointer-width native Koffi string decoding. Threaded the already-derived pointerSize into readUtf16. Reworked the fake Koffi environment around numeric BigInt addresses and pointer buffers, added assertions for pointer-width serialization and COM deallocation, and added real-Koffi resultPath cases for representative UTF-16 and long-string behavior. Added a bilingual implementation note recording the decoding and ownership constraints.
call_sites: loadWin32DialogBindings derives pointerSize with koffi.sizeof('void *'), passes it to readUtf16 in resultPath, then frees the unchanged GetDisplayName address with CoTaskMemFree and releases the IShellItem in finally.

runFolderDialog consumes dialog.resultPath after a successful Show, checks its HRESULT, and returns the decoded path to the directory-picker caller while retaining dialog and COM cleanup in finally blocks.
tests: Parameterized fake-Koffi tests exercise both four-byte and eight-byte BigInt addresses, assert that the decoder receives the matching pointer-buffer width, and assert that CoTaskMemFree receives the original address.

Real-Koffi resultPath tests decode live UTF-16 buffers containing zero-low-byte BMP code units, a surrogate pair, more than 32 KiB of text, and an embedded NUL; they compare the serialized pointer before native dereference and verify deallocation and COM cleanup.

title: Surface provider HTTP error bodies hidden by opaque SDK messages
before: Provider error handlers generally derived errorMessage only from Error.message or JSON.stringify(error). When proxies or gateways returned non-schema 4xx/5xx responses, SDK objects retained the HTTP status and response body in fields such as status, error, $metadata, or $response, but pi discarded those fields. Users therefore saw opaque text such as "403 status code (no body)" or "Unknown: UnknownError" instead of the gateway's actual reason. OpenAI Completions also appended OpenRouter metadata.raw unconditionally, risking duplicate text.
after: A shared provider-error normalizer extracts status and body data across Mistral-, OpenAI-, Google-, and Bedrock-shaped errors, safely serializes non-Error throws, ignores empty bodies, caps surfaced bodies at 4000 characters, and detects when the SDK message already contains the body. Eight provider paths now use normalized formatting, preserving provider prefixes and Bedrock's retention hint while exposing status plus body when the original message is opaque. OpenAI Completions appends metadata.raw only when it is not already present.
diff: The change adds packages/ai/src/utils/error-body.ts with normalizeProviderError, formatProviderError, safe JSON serialization, SDK-field probing, duplicate-body detection, and bounded truncation. It replaces message-only formatting in Azure OpenAI Responses, Bedrock Converse, Google Generative AI, Google Vertex, OpenAI Codex Responses, OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and OpenRouter Images. Three test files cover helper behavior and real provider catch paths for image, text, status-prefixed, and Bedrock errors, including preservation and deduplication cases.
call_sites: Azure OpenAI Responses, Google Generative AI, Google Vertex, OpenAI Codex Responses, OpenAI Responses, and OpenRouter Images now compose displayed errors with normalizeProviderError and formatProviderError.
OpenAI Completions now uses normalized formatting and only appends OpenRouter metadata.raw when the formatted message does not already include it.
Bedrock formatting uses normalized status/body data when the SDK message is body-blind, while retaining service-exception prefixes and the existing data-retention documentation hint.
tests: Unit tests cover Mistral-, OpenAI-, Google-, and Bedrock-shaped errors, non-Error throws, empty parsed bodies, truncation, duplicate-body detection, prefix formatting, and message preservation.

The OpenRouter image regression test injects an OpenAI-shaped 403 error whose parsed body contains a gateway reason and asserts that output includes both 403 and the reason rather than only the opaque SDK message.

Provider-level regression tests exercise OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Bedrock catch paths, asserting status/body passthrough, preservation of the OpenAI prefix, elimination of Unknown: UnknownError, and single occurrence of OpenRouter metadata.raw.

limitations: No fabricated GitHub discussion metadata; implementation evidence must come from local git and checkout.

episode.title: Surface provider HTTP error bodies hidden by opaque SDK messages
episode.before: Provider error handlers generally derived errorMessage only from Error.message or JSON.stringify(error). When proxies or gateways returned non-schema 4xx/5xx responses, SDK objects retained the HTTP status and response body in fields such as status, error, $metadata, or $response, but pi discarded those fields. Users therefore saw opaque text such as "403 status code (no body)" or "Unknown: UnknownError" instead of the gateway's actual reason. OpenAI Completions also appended OpenRouter metadata.raw unconditionally, risking duplicate text.
episode.after: A shared provider-error normalizer extracts status and body data across Mistral-, OpenAI-, Google-, and Bedrock-shaped errors, safely serializes non-Error throws, ignores empty bodies, caps surfaced bodies at 4000 characters, and detects when the SDK message already contains the body. Eight provider paths now use normalized formatting, preserving provider prefixes and Bedrock's retention hint while exposing status plus body when the original message is opaque. OpenAI Completions appends metadata.raw only when it is not already present.
episode.diff: The change adds packages/ai/src/utils/error-body.ts with normalizeProviderError, formatProviderError, safe JSON serialization, SDK-field probing, duplicate-body detection, and bounded truncation. It replaces message-only formatting in Azure OpenAI Responses, Bedrock Converse, Google Generative AI, Google Vertex, OpenAI Codex Responses, OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and OpenRouter Images. Three test files cover helper behavior and real provider catch paths for image, text, status-prefixed, and Bedrock errors, including preservation and deduplication cases.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned merge commit 6fbeba51 merged PR #5832; its implementation commit 62fad94f states that eight provider paths were routed through a shared normalizer to close issue #5763.

normalizeProviderError extracts numeric status from statusCode, status, $metadata.httpStatusCode, or $response.statusCode and extracts a body from body, a non-empty parsed error object, or $response.body.
The normalizer safely serializes non-Error values, records whether the existing message already contains the body, trims bodies, and truncates them at a 4000-character cap.

formatProviderError preserves the existing message when it already carries the body or lacks extractable status/body; otherwise it emits status plus body and optionally retains a provider-specific prefix.

Before the change, OpenRouter Images, OpenAI Completions, Google providers, and OpenAI Codex Responses used only error.message or JSON serialization, while Azure/OpenAI Responses formatted status with error.message and Bedrock formatted only error.message; these paths could omit SDK-held response bodies.

Azure OpenAI Responses, Google Generative AI, Google Vertex, OpenAI Codex Responses, OpenAI Responses, and OpenRouter Images now compose displayed errors with normalizeProviderError and formatProviderError.
OpenAI Completions now uses normalized formatting and only appends OpenRouter metadata.raw when the formatted message does not already include it.
Bedrock formatting uses normalized status/body data when the SDK message is body-blind, while retaining service-exception prefixes and the existing data-retention documentation hint.
Unit tests cover Mistral-, OpenAI-, Google-, and Bedrock-shaped errors, non-Error throws, empty parsed bodies, truncation, duplicate-body detection, prefix formatting, and message preservation.

The OpenRouter image regression test injects an OpenAI-shaped 403 error whose parsed body contains a gateway reason and asserts that output includes both 403 and the reason rather than only the opaque SDK message.

Provider-level regression tests exercise OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Bedrock catch paths, asserting status/body passthrough, preservation of the OpenAI prefix, elimination of Unknown: UnknownError, and single occurrence of OpenRouter metadata.raw.
Relative to the merge commit's first parent, the implementation changes 12 AI-package files with 580 insertions and 36 deletions, including one shared utility and three new test files.

title: Make declared custom-provider display names and API protocols editable
before: At parent c172faed370bb62a0b0ef2a04b76bdc87f5f63c6, the Models page could collect a custom provider's displayName and route-level API protocol during creation, but ProviderEditor did not receive the directory entry's declared status and its customized section exposed only the existing credential, endpoint, and model controls. Reopening a hand-declared pi-ai route therefore could not edit the two route-owned fields. Save confirmation also retained the display name captured when the editor opened, so it could announce the old name after a rename.
after: At merge commit 9c06f682c409ce4922442bd8e14fca30d7485b0e, ModelsSection propagates row.entry.declared into ProviderEditor. For declared pi-ai routes only, ProviderEditor renders an editable display-name input and API-protocol select, obtains protocol choices from the adapter namespace schema, represents a missing protocol with a localized unselected option, and persists changes through the existing minimal path-operation mutation flow. Clearing the display name unsets the stored override so lower configuration layers or the route id can supply the fallback. After applying changes, ModelsSection reloads the provider directory before publishing its saved notice and resolves the current display name by stable provider id. Both custom-provider protocol selects use the shared select styling.
diff: The implementation adds an optional declared flag to editor targets and ProviderEditorProps; copies the directory's declared marker through target construction and rendering; imports and reuses protocolChoices; conditionally adds displayName and api controls when the editor is for a declared pi-ai route; adds localized copy for an unset protocol; applies the shared selectInput class to protocol dropdowns; and changes save-notice sequencing to reload and resolve the refreshed identity before announcement. Unit tests cover field visibility, rename set/unset operations, composition-layer fallback, refreshed save copy, protocol mutation, and missing-protocol selection. A browser test reopens a declared route, verifies its original name and protocol, changes both, checks the refreshed row and notice, and verifies settings.yaml. An accessibility snapshot records the expanded editor, and a style test prevents bare native-arrow selects.
call_sites: ModelsSection copies row.entry.declared into EditorTarget and passes it to ProviderEditor, connecting directory classification to conditional editor behavior.
tests: Provider form tests establish that declared-route editors expose display name and protocol fields; rename emits a displayName set operation; whitespace clearing emits an unset operation; a composition-provided name becomes the placeholder; protocol changes emit the expected mutation; a missing protocol remains unselected; and the saved notice uses the refreshed directory name.

The Web end-to-end test reopens Acme Gateway, verifies openai-completions and Acme Gateway, changes them to anthropic-messages and Acme 网关, waits for the renamed row and save notice, then verifies both values in settings.yaml.
The declared-edit accessibility snapshot records the declared provider editor with display-name textbox, API-address textbox, and API-protocol combobox containing the three schema-derived protocols.
The styles test scans client TSX select elements and fails if any lacks selectInput, guarding the shared chevron styling used by both protocol dropdowns.

title: Clean the working tree when update autostash restoration conflicts
before: During `hermes update`, `cmd_update` stashed local changes, pulled updates, and called `_restore_stashed_changes` from a `finally` block. The restore helper treated only a nonzero `git stash apply` exit status as failure. On failure it printed recovery guidance and exited, but left partially applied files and conflict markers in the updated working tree. after: After applying the stash, `_restore_stashed_changes` queries Git for unmerged paths with `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`. If stash application fails or unmerged paths exist, it runs `git reset --hard HEAD`, reports that the tree was reset, retains the stash for manual recovery, and exits with status 1. diff: The issue-bearing commit `3ab50376b0b71c39cb3575a4186b112d4b59e1c3`, included by pinned merge `55510cbad209c7fac6d3d94019aeeedecfea7754`, changes `hermes_cli/main.py` to add an unmerged-file probe and a hard-reset cleanup branch around stash restoration. before: `simple_send_with_retries` returned `None` when the summarizer response was invalid. `ChatSummary.summarize_all` immediately concatenated that value with `prompts.summary_prefix`, causing an implicit `TypeError` inside the background summarization thread. `Coder.summarize_worker` neither classified nor reported the failure through the normal I/O error channel.

title: Reject prompts while manual session compaction is active
before: AgentSession.prompt() did not check the manual-compaction state. After compact() set _compactionAbortController, a concurrent interactive or RPC prompt could continue through input handling, expansion, authentication, compaction checks, message construction, and agent execution while compact() was rebuilding session context. The RPC call site would report success once prompt preflight completed.
after: AgentSession.prompt() checks whether _compactionAbortController is defined immediately after extension-command dispatch. A normal prompt submitted during manual compaction throws a retryable instruction before input interception or message construction. The existing prompt catch path reports preflight failure, allowing RPC mode to return an error instead of acknowledging the prompt. Extension commands remain eligible for immediate dispatch because their handling precedes the guard.
diff: Added a six-line manual-compaction guard to AgentSession.prompt(). Added a characterization test that holds session_before_compact open and verifies a concurrent prompt throws. Added an issue-specific RPC regression test verifying preflightResult is false, the prompt errors, no probe message reaches in-memory or persisted session history, and no agent_start or agent_settled events occur.
call_sites: RPC prompt handling starts session.prompt() asynchronously, emits success only when preflight reports true, and emits an error from the rejected promise when preflight has not succeeded. Therefore the new guard becomes an RPC error response without changing RPC-mode code.
tests: The prompt characterization test pauses session_before_compact, submits a third prompt during that interval, and expects the exact compaction-in-progress error before releasing compaction.

The issue #7150 RPC regression test verifies the rejected prompt reports preflightResult=false, returns a compaction error, is absent from agent and persisted user messages, and emits neither agent_start nor agent_settled.

title: Surface max-token turn endings as a persistent localized truncation notice
before: At parent commit 185a1f7da3b042319a8ef3fb0aca48a08ca78ae6, the session log already represented provider output-cap termination as `turn/end` with `reason.kind === 'max-tokens'`, but the Web conversation pipeline had no corresponding node definition, runtime node type, or renderer. Only terminal errors produced a dedicated turn-ending row, so truncated assistant output appeared to be a normal completion and remained unexplained after live display, reload, or history replay.
after: At a995fc27061cee676f36be14bdf6b5fc2f33e618, `turn/end` events with `reason.kind === 'max-tokens'` produce a durable `turn-max-tokens` conversation node. The node is anchored after the closing assistant output but before the turn tail, preserving the tail's branch action. A keyed renderer displays a warning dot with localized English and Chinese text explaining that the reply was cut off, earlier output remains, and the user can send "continue". The same event-derived definition reconstructs the notice during window rebuild and history replay, while completed and error turns remain distinct.
diff: The change added `TurnMaxTokensNode` to the public conversation-node union; introduced and registered a `turnMaxTokensDefinition` that matches only max-token `turn/end` events, records turn/sequence/time/last-step data, and computes an anchor before the turn tail; registered the new node kind with the chat snapshot builder and keyed renderer; added warning-row styling and locale-owned English/Chinese copy; extended the fixture session with a truncated max-token turn; and added definition, renderer, and assembled Web snapshot coverage for matching, exclusion of completed/error turns, replay from a window lacking `turn/start`, node ordering, localized presentation, and retained partial output.
call_sites: The new definition and renderer are wired into the normal conversation pipeline, and the legacy chat snapshot builder recognizes `turn-max-tokens` as a finalized contribution.
tests: Definition tests verify that max-token endings materialize the notice, error and completed endings do not, the notice is ordered between truncated assistant output and the turn tail, and replay still works when the loaded window starts after the owning `turn/start`.

title: Make the compression context floor configurable with a 16K safety minimum
before: Compression thresholds were always floored at the fixed MINIMUM_CONTEXT_LENGTH value of 64,000 tokens. ContextCompressor used that constant during construction and model updates, and the auxiliary compression-model feasibility check rejected every auxiliary model below 64,000 tokens. There was no compression.minimum_context_floor setting, and gateway agent-cache signatures could not react to changes to such a setting.
after: Agent initialization reads compression.minimum_context_floor, coerces valid values to an integer, and otherwise retains the 64,000-token default. A shared helper computes the effective floor, clamping configured values to a hard safety minimum of 16,000 tokens. ContextCompressor stores and applies that effective floor both during construction and update_model threshold recalculation. Auxiliary compression models are validated against the same effective floor, so a deliberately lowered floor permits a smaller auxiliary context window. The gateway includes the setting in its cache-busting configuration so edits rebuild cached agents.
diff: Added _MINIMUM_CONTEXT_FLOOR_HARD_LIMIT and get_configurable_minimum_context in model_metadata; parsed and forwarded compression.minimum_context_floor from init_agent; extended ContextCompressor with a minimum_context_floor argument and passed the resolved floor into _compute_threshold_tokens at initialization and model updates; replaced the auxiliary model's fixed 64K feasibility requirement with the compressor's effective floor; added the setting to gateway cache-signature inputs; and added tests covering defaults, explicit floors, 16K clamping, threshold behavior, model updates, smaller auxiliary-model acceptance, and gateway cache invalidation.
call_sites: The auxiliary compression-model feasibility check obtains the effective floor from agent.context_compressor and rejects an auxiliary context window only when it is below that floor, replacing the previous fixed 64K comparison.
GatewayRunner includes compression.minimum_context_floor among construction-time configuration keys that invalidate its cached agent.
tests: New unit tests verify the default 64K floor, explicit configured values, clamping values below 16K, initial threshold behavior, floor dominance at low percentages, and preservation of the floor after update_model.
The auxiliary feasibility test demonstrates that a 32,000-token configured floor allows a 32,768-token auxiliary model and auto-lowers the live threshold to that auxiliary context size.
Gateway tests verify extraction of compression.minimum_context_floor and that changing it from 64,000 to 32,000 changes the cached-agent configuration signature.
